paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this whole passage: people keep pointing at Jesus. John the Baptist says, "Look, the Lamb of God!" (John 1:36). Andrew finds his brother and says, "We have found the Messiah" (John 1:41). Philip finds Nathanael and says the same kind of thing (John 1:45). Nobody in this passage is the star of the show, and that's the whole point.

And look at HOW they point. When Nathanael doubts, Philip doesn't argue him down or give a speech. He says, "Come and see" (John 1:46), the same words Jesus gave the first two followers (John 1:39). I think that's a relief, baker. You don't have to win the debate, you just have to bring somebody close to Jesus. I spent years in the back of a drawer with zero answers for anybody, so trust me, you're more qualified than you feel!

Then comes the best part, because Jesus is the One who really sees. He knew who Simon was (John 1:42), and He saw Nathanael under the fig tree before Philip ever called him (John 1:48). Jesus promised him, "You will see greater things than these" (John 1:50). So come close, baker, and bring somebody with you. The fig tree was just the trailer, and Jesus still has more to show you.
